---
title: Visualizing a graph
---



## Utility scripts

`udsyntax` includes Python functions and utility scripts to create diagrams of `SyntaxGraph`s.

### Requirements

- `udsyntax` and the spaCy pipeline for whichever `--lang` you pass, already installed
- local install of `graphviz` to render a png file

Install `dot`:

Mac OS:

    brew install graphviz

Windows: download from https://graphviz.org/download/ or

    winget install --id Graphviz.Graphviz

Verify it worked: print a version string.

    dot -V


### Scripts

`text_to_dot.py`: analyze and graph a string

```bash
python scripts/text_to_dot.py "Gallia est omnis divisa in partes tres." --lang la | dot -Tpng -o bg_1_1.png
```


`corpus_to_dot.py`: identify a passage by URN, analyze it, generate its dot representation


```bash
python3 scripts/corpus_to_dot.py scratch/data/compnov.cex --urn "urn:cts:compnov:bible.genesis.vulgate:1.1" --lang la | dot -Tpng -o genesis_1_1.png
```

Parameters:

- `corpus` (positional, one or more): CEX files (`urn|text` lines) to search, read and concatenated in the order given via `udsyntax.read_cex_many`.
- `--urn` (required): the exact URN of the passage to select (via the new `udsyntax.select_urn`, an exact match, not the substring `urn_filter` that `read_cex`/`read_cex_many` accept). If more than one line across the given files shares this URN, a warning goes to stderr and the first one is used. If none matches, the script exits with an error naming the URN and the files searched.
- `--lang` / `-l` (required): `la` for Latin (`la_core_web_lg`) or `grc` for Ancient Greek (`grc_dep_web_lg`).



## Composing diagrams from Python

`udsyntax` includes two functions, `to_mermaid()` and `to_dot()`, that diagram a `SyntaxGraph` using the syntax of Mermaid or the open-source `graphviz` package.


```python
graph = SyntaxGraph.from_doc(doc)

print(graph.to_mermaid())                  # "graph BT" ... (root-at-top tree)
print(graph.to_mermaid(orientation="LR"))  # left-to-right instead

print(graph.to_dot())                      # a Graphviz "digraph { ... }"
print(graph.to_dot(orientation="LR"))      # left-to-right instead 
```
